title: Selected Nancay waits from FRB 20220912A show no clear serial dependence after session control
abstract: We test adjacent detected waits from FRB 20220912A with public Nancay data. Filename times and an exposure log avoid rounded summary times and off-source gaps. After we join detections less than one second apart, 21 selected sessions give 535 waits and 514 adjacent pairs. The correlation of session-centered log waits is -0.0923. A conditional within-session permutation test gives a two-sided p-value of 0.2316. Two other join rules and a local-block control also do not cross 0.05. Synthetic rank-order tests detect an illustrative latent serial correlation of plus or minus 0.2 in more than 96 percent of trials. This is a null result for one statistic, not proof of random emission. Missed bursts, session selection, short-time grouping and untested nonlinear memory limit the result. No new physical signal is established. Code, exact external input hashes, aggregate results, permutation statistics and a retrieval recipe support reproduction.

display.caption: Observed adjacent wait correlation and conditional permutation controls. Negative correlation also occurs under the null because each finite group is centered.
